correctness.rationale: The exact canonical edge condition is \((N-a)b\le T_N\). Its increasing greedy successor dominates every feasible successor path, so the shortest canonical subcycle equals a one-dimensional hitting time. For both parities, centering at half the face count gives an exact integer recurrence with increment \(1+\lfloor Q_m(j)\rfloor\). Solving \(Q_m(j)=r\) shows that the two components of each fixed increment band have total width \(2\sqrt m(\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt r)+O_r(1)\); crossing a band takes that width divided by \(r+1\), up to bounded endpoint effects. A dyadic lower bound on the outer increments gives \(O(\sqrt m/A+\log m)\) steps outside \(|j|\le A\sqrt m\), so the convergent series is the full asymptotic. The universal lower constant follows from the source theorem through the exact tangent identity, not from finite computation.

value.rationale: The motivating source introduces \(n(N)\), proves only square-root-order bounds, and explicitly compares its easy shortened construction with shorter canonical subcycles numerically through \(N=10^8\). The theorem explains that persistent gap by an exact lattice-sensitive series constant, reduces the canonical asymptotic upper coefficient from the source\'s coarse value below \(5\) to \(2.630472693388697\ldots\), and sharpens the universal lower coefficient to \(\pi/\sqrt2\). This directly advances a natural invariant highlighted by the source rather than extending a finite census.
